name: usage-chart
summary: A chart of numbers over time for up to five series, as stacked bars, lines or stacked areas, with a legend, hover details and the same numbers as a table for screen readers.
useWhen: People need to see how something changed over days or weeks, such as credits spent per tool or generations per day.
A usage, billing or analytics page needs more than one total: the shape over time matters.

alternatives.name: usage-summary
alternatives.when: one period's totals and a history table are enough; its single stacked bar says how the total splits

alternatives.name: progress
alternatives.when: there is one number against one limit, such as credits left this month

alternatives.name: table
alternatives.when: people need the exact figures to compare and sort, not the trend

rules.do: Use bars to compare totals between days, lines to compare trends between series, and areas to show how a total is made up over time.
rules.dont: Use lines for stacked totals or areas for unrelated series; the shape then suggests something the numbers do not say.

rules.do: Show up to five series, the number of chart colors, and fold the rest into "Other".
rules.dont: Add a sixth color or reuse one; two series in the same color cannot be told apart.

rules.do: Keep each series in the same position everywhere in an app, so it always gets the same color.
rules.dont: Reorder series between charts; people learn "lime is Image studio" once.

rules.do: Pass `unit` (credits, generations, minutes) and put the period in the description.
rules.dont: Leave bare numbers on the axis with no word for what they count.

a11y: The chart is a figure named by its title. The same numbers follow as a real table with a caption, column headers and row headers, for screen readers.
The drawing can be focused with Tab and stepped through with the left and right arrow keys, which shows each step's details the way hovering does.
The legend is text next to each color, so series are never told apart by color alone.
Axis labels use the secondary text color, which meets 4.5:1 on the card.
The chart does not animate when it appears or changes.
